title: Adaptive vendor scorecard and experiment roadmap for regional model sourcing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: As Redwood expands regionally and supports Dedicated/Private deployments, we need a repeatable way to evaluate and compare model vendors (open and commercial) across cost, latency, reliability, regulatory fit, and quality. Current spreadsheets are ad-hoc, stale, and do not capture dynamic signals like short-term capacity constraints or model degradations.

Goal: Deliver an adaptive vendor scorecard (AVS) and a prioritized experiment roadmap that: 1) quantifies trade-offs for region-specific procurement decisions, 2) surfaces substitution triggers (when to fallback to alternate vendors/models), and 3) provides playbook inputs for commercial negotiations (SLA/penalty thresholds).

Scope: Build scorecard schema (weights + metrics), implement routine signals ingestion (latency, p99, cost-per-token, recent eval regressions, availability incidents), define contract trigger thresholds, run 3 regional pilot experiments (NA, EU, APAC) to validate scoring and substitution latency, and produce negotiation playbook artifacts for Sales and Legal.
acceptance_criteria: Scorecard schema documented in Confluence with metric definitions and default weights
Automated ingestion pipeline (daily) populating the scorecard dashboard from metrics sources (console telemetry, infra logs, third-party provider status) in a staging dashboard
Pilot experiments executed in NA and EU: measured substitution latency and user-facing error rate across 2 workload profiles (search-heavy, chat-heavy)
Negotiation playbook drafted with three contract templates and recommended SLA/penalty thresholds based on pilot results
Handoff ticket to Sales/Legal with executive summary and reproducible notebook for weight tuning
tasks: Design scorecard metrics and initial weighting (PM + Research)
Instrument signal collection: perf metrics (p50/p95/p99), cost-per-1k tokens, availability, eval-accuracy deltas
Build staging dashboard (Console) for vendor comparison by region
Define substitution experiment plan and rollback criteria
Run pilot substitution experiments in NA and EU; collect telemetry
Analyze pilot, tune weights, and produce negotiation playbook
Create handoff docs and training for Sales/Legal
comments: 2026-02-16 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes added to Drive (link below). Agreed to prioritize NA and EU pilots before APAC due to higher immediate contract cadence.

2026-03-02 - Research: Ran lightweight evals on three open models + two commercial APIs; initial quality deltas captured in eval-notebook.ipynb. Suggest moving spell-check tolerance into quality metric to avoid penalizing small formatting differences.
2026-03-08 - Legal (Nora Singh): Requested explicit language for fallback behavior and data residency constraints in playbook. Added to negotiation checklist.
decisions: Use composite score of performance (30%), cost (25%), availability (20%), eval-quality (20%), regulatory fit (5%) as starting weights
Pilot will run substitution at request-routing layer with soft-beta traffic at 5% -> 25% ramp if no regressions
Fallback decision window set to 60s for substitution; graceful degradation preferred over hard failures
Negotiation thresholds: SLA targets to be derived from pilot p95 and p99 metrics plus 2x safety margin
risks: Signal freshness: daily ingestion may miss short-lived capacity outages; consider real-time alerts for severe incidents
Model quality drift: weekly evals might not detect rapid regressions caused by prompt shifts
Vendor pushback on transparent telemetry sharing; some commercial providers may limit observability
Customer churn risk if substitution causes increased latency or quality regressions during experiments
